learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.outcome: Controls unlocked; instruction to play 50 then 500 more
50 games, average $4.4, median $2, biggest $32, profit -$780; line below price
550 games, average $25.8, median $4, biggest $8192, profit +$3182; visible spike and outlying flip-13 contribution
Same 550 games and payout average retained; profit +$13082 and dashed price line lowered

observations.action: Opened Show me why and scrolled
observations.outcome: Prediction held; reveal ties $8192 to 58% of payouts, each flip contributes $1 expected, 20 flips $20; nine unseen outcomes gave zero sample contribution and 75% pay $4 or less

prediction.reason: Clear finite rule and plausible price commitments.

interaction.reason: More games exposes rare-outcome jump; changing price isolates profit from payout.

payoff.reason: Uses actual sample and contribution strip to connect expectation to unstable averages and typical low outcomes.

clarity.reason: Rules, counters and highlighted controls legible; vertical scroll reaches explanation.

transfer.reason: Expected contribution principle stated, but no new application or applicability exercise.

surprise.reason: Committed fair price holds but typical outcomes and sample jump provide expectation tension.

visualExplanation.reason: Running average and per-flip contribution bars carry rare-event explanation.

playfulness.reason: Repeated sampling and price switching enable exploration; no reset observed.

practicalValue.reason: Distinguishes entry cost, expected payout and typical outcome for this game.

depth.reason: Expectation, median, sample instability and price-dependent profit are linked.

complexity.reason: Links probability times payout, sums across 20 outcomes, and contrasts median with expectation.
complexity.conceptualDemand: balanced: supported linked relations; fractions and averages required
complexity.interfaceBurden: low: labelled discrete controls; no notation input

whyCool: Adding 500 games makes a rare $8192 win visibly dominate the contribution strip and move the running average above the entry price.
caveat: One random path; changing price recomputes profit over retained games, and there is no new-case transfer task.
missingEvidence: Phone, keyboard-only, focus, contrast measurement, zoom/reflow and reduced motion untested
screenshots: Inline observed browser screenshots at 50 games and revealed 550-game state; no saved image file
